title: Microsoft October 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,411 flaws, 3 zero-days
summary: Microsoft's October 2026 Patch Tuesday addresses a record-breaking 1,411 vulnerabilities, including three zero-day flaws with one actively exploited. Administrators should apply the latest updates to secure Windows and other affected Microsoft products.

also_covered.title: Microsoft releases Windows 10 KB5126657 extended security update
Windows 11 KB5127648 & KB5126653 cumulative updates released

action: Apply the October 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates, including KB5126657, KB5127648, and KB5126653, to address the vulnerabilities.

title: Docker Hub flaw let attackers impersonate users, tamper with images
summary: Docker disclosed a critical vulnerability in Docker Hub that allowed attackers to use personal access tokens to access, push, pull, or delete container repositories belonging to other users. Docker has already fixed the flaw and reported no evidence of active exploitation.

also_covered.title: Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another

action: Review container repositories for unauthorized changes and ensure account security practices are up to date, as Docker has already fixed the issue on their end.

title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access, Only Two Patched So Far
summary: An attacker chained three zero-day vulnerabilities in Ivanti Connect Secure to gain unauthenticated root access, and the vendor has released patches for only two of the flaws. Because these flaws are actively exploited, affected organizations face significant risk while awaiting a patch for the third bug.

also_covered.title: Ivanti warns of Connect Secure zero-day exploited in attacks

action: Update Ivanti Connect Secure to the patched release immediately and monitor systems for signs of compromise, noting that a fix for the third vulnerability is still pending.

title: SAP Discloses Critical CVSS 10 Flaw in Cloud SDK for Python Allowing OAuth2 Credential Theft
summary: SAP disclosed a critical flaw in its Cloud SDK for Python that allows attackers to steal OAuth2 client credentials from multi-tenant applications on the SAP Business Technology Platform. This vulnerability poses a significant risk as it affects authentication security for applications utilizing the SDK.
action: Review the SAP security advisory from October 13 and apply the necessary patches or updates provided by SAP to secure multi-tenant applications.

title: Windows 11 KB5127648 & KB5126653 cumulative updates released
summary: Microsoft has released Patch Tuesday cumulative updates for multiple versions of Windows 11 to fix security vulnerabilities, bugs, and introduce new features. System administrators should apply these updates to maintain system security and stability.

title: GitHub Tightens npm Publishing After Flaw Left 1,500+ Packages Vulnerable to Hijacking
summary: GitHub has implemented a 48-hour expiration policy for unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations to prevent unauthorized package hijacking. This change mitigates a flaw that allowed attackers to push new versions to other users' packages without stealing credentials.
action: Ensure that your npm trusted publishing configurations are successfully used to publish within 48 hours of creation to validate them and exempt them from automatic expiration.

title: Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers
summary: Attackers remotely hijacked Danfoss refrigeration controllers at hundreds of French supermarkets, raising temperatures to 50 degrees Celsius and forcing food disposal. This incident highlights the physical security risks of remote management access for industrial and commercial IoT devices.
action: Review and secure remote management access to Danfoss controllers, ensuring strong authentication and restricting external exposure.

title: UK Housing Ombudsman Service investigates 'security incident'
summary: The U.K. Housing Ombudsman Service is investigating a third-party IT security incident that impacted its case management system. The disruption highlights the ongoing risks organizations face through third-party vendor dependencies.

title: TFG London cyberattack disrupts systems at Hobbs and Whistles retailers
summary: TFG London detected a cybersecurity incident that disrupted IT systems across its Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles fashion retail brands. The attack highlights ongoing threats to retail sector infrastructure and customer-facing operations.

title: The MFA Gaps Attackers are Still Exploiting
summary: Attackers continue to exploit gaps in multi-factor authentication by using stolen credentials to target unprotected VPNs, RDP, and Windows systems. This highlights the risk of securing only cloud applications while leaving legacy or internal access points reliant on passwords alone.

title: LG Smart TVs Vulnerable to Pre-Auth Root Takeover From Local Network
summary: Three chained vulnerabilities in LG's webOS allow local network attackers to gain root access to affected smart TVs without user interaction. LG has released a firmware update to patch the flaws.

title: Anthropic warns self-replicating AI could spread to your smart devices
summary: Anthropic warns that small AI models could soon gain the ability to self-replicate across consumer IoT devices like smart ovens and Android TV boxes. This capability could lead to distributed, self-propagating botnets that are difficult to shut down due to a lack of centralized infrastructure.

also_covered.title: Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Soon Form Self-Propagating IoT Botnets

title: Microsoft: Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro reached end of support
summary: Microsoft announced that Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro editions have reached their end of support, meaning they will no longer receive monthly security updates. This matters because running unsupported operating systems exposes devices to unpatched security vulnerabilities and potential exploitation over time.

title: Xandr Fined a Record €8.6 Million for Relaying Grindr Data Revealing Sexual Orientation
summary: The Norwegian Data Protection Authority fined Microsoft's Xandr €8.6 million for illegally relaying sensitive Grindr user data to advertisers. The penalty is the largest ever issued by the watchdog due to the severe nature of the privacy breach.

title: [Webinar] How to Stop AI-Driven Privilege Escalation With Runtime Identity Controls
summary: This is a promotional webinar announcement about stopping AI-driven privilege escalation using runtime identity controls. It provides no specific threat intelligence, vulnerability disclosures, or actionable security incidents.

title: Product Walkthrough: Bitdefender AI Visibility and Control
summary: This article discusses a product walkthrough for Bitdefender AI Visibility and Control. It highlights the growing challenges organizations face in tracking browser-based chat assistants, editor extensions, and local model runtimes.
